title: JPEG export
objective: Write a saved entry's exact render to a new JPEG without touching the original, from the desktop and the API.
context_summary: Implements the accepted export contract (quality 90, native picker, never overwrite, metadata stripped by default with Keep metadata) as designed in docs/design/export.md. The export lane uses the existing lane runner; folding it into one job table stays with that work.

tasks.description: Read the original's supported EXIF fields once at source preparation and write the export's own EXIF segment.
extra_context: The reader runs on the source worker over bytes it already read; it never fails a preparation.
An independent parser (kamadak-exif, already in the lockfile) reads back what the writer writes, in tests only.

context_links.label: Export design
context_links.relevance: Behavior, destination rules, metadata table, API and proposals.

context_links.label: Source preparation
context_links.relevance: JPEG and RAW preparation, where the capture metadata is read and carried.

acceptance_criteria: `CaptureMetadata::from_jpeg` and `from_raw` read exactly the design's field table from JPEG APP1, NEF/DNG TIFF and a RAF's embedded JPEG, bounded, dropping fields of the wrong type or count.
`exif_payload` writes the kept fields plus Orientation 1, ColorSpace sRGB, pixel dimensions, ExifVersion and Software, and no thumbnail, maker note or serial number.
The prepared JPEG and RAW sources carry their capture metadata without a second read of the original.

steps: Round-trip synthetic EXIF written by an independent writer through the reader and the export writer, and read the result back independently.
Malformed, truncated, looping and oversized IFDs yield empty or partial metadata without panicking.
expected_results: Every kept field round-trips; every excluded field is absent; malformed input never panics.

tasks.description: Encode a rendered frame as a baseline quality-90 JPEG with an sRGB profile, and stage and publish it without replacing anything.
extra_context: The encoder streams into the staged file; no whole encoded buffer exists.
Publishing uses a hard link, which fails if the name exists, and falls back to an exclusive create and copy.

context_links.label: Export design
context_links.relevance: Behavior, destination rules, metadata table, API and proposals.

context_links.label: Durable file writes
context_links.relevance: The crate's existing sync helpers; its publish replaces, which export must not.

acceptance_criteria: `encode_jpeg` writes quality 90, the ICC profile `profile::check` accepts, the optional EXIF segment, reports progress and stops on cancel.
`Destination::check` refuses every existing path, symlink and wrong extension or parent; `publish` never replaces a file that appeared after the check.
Failure, cancellation and dropping a staged file leave no temporary file behind.

steps: Decode encoded fixtures independently and compare within a stated tolerance; inspect markers, profile and EXIF.
Exercise every destination refusal and a race where the destination appears before publish.
expected_results: Output decodes at the frame's size within tolerance; no existing file is ever modified.

tasks.description: Run export as a job: freeze the target on the owner, render and write it on an export lane, and expose export.plan, export.jpeg, export.read and export.cancel.
extra_context: Plan on the owner in O(layers), as analysis.request does; render on the lane with the exact phase.
The lane never supersedes a job; one running and four waiting per lane.

context_links.label: Export design
context_links.relevance: Behavior, destination rules, metadata table, API and proposals.

context_links.label: Lane runner
context_links.relevance: The lane runner, progress and panic containment the export lane uses.

context_links.label: Method table
context_links.relevance: Where the four methods and their schemas are declared.

acceptance_criteria: A later commit never changes an accepted export; a retried request id writes one file.
Progress and cancellation reach the activity board and export.read; a finished export records an event.
Unavailable providers, missing originals and unprepared sources refuse explicitly; exported bytes equal an independent render_entry of the same entry after decoding within tolerance.

steps: Drive the owner through the in-process client over JPEG and RAW fixtures, both metadata modes, concurrent commits, cancellation and every refusal.
expected_results: Every behavior in the design's API table holds through the JSON method table.

tasks.description: Export from the desktop: the title bar's Export menu, Cmd+E and Shift+Cmd+E, palette entries, the native save dialog and status, with an export smoke scenario.
extra_context: The desktop holds no export logic: it asks export.plan, opens the dialog and sends export.jpeg.
Evidence runs bypass the native dialog with a scripted destination.

context_links.label: Export design
context_links.relevance: Behavior, destination rules, metadata table, API and proposals.

context_links.label: Develop workspace
context_links.relevance: Title bar, keyboard and palette conventions.

context_links.label: Smoke scenarios
context_links.relevance: Where the export scenario is registered.

acceptance_criteria: The menu, shortcuts and palette send the same export.jpeg the API documents, for the displayed entry.
The status bar shows exporting, exported and refused states; the Performance section shows the running job.
An `export` smoke scenario captures the menu and the exported state and verifies the written file independently.

steps: Run the export smoke scenario against a current release build and inspect its captures, state and logs.
expected_results: Captures, state and the written JPEG agree.

tasks.description: Verify export end to end on the M4 Mac, measure it, and update the specs, feature status and user guide.
extra_context: Timing runs happen once, after the feature is complete, per performance rule 13.

acceptance_criteria: Wall time and peak memory for 24 and 60 MP JPEG and one RAW per camera are recorded with scope.
RAW exports from NEF and RAF verified independently in both metadata modes with originals unchanged.
Specs, feature status, user guide and roadmap describe the delivered behavior.

steps: Run verify rendered once on the integrated branch, then the export measurement.
expected_results: A passing rendered tier and recorded measurements.
